Namespace: Platform.Data.Doublets Forked from: Konard/LinksPlatform/Platform/Platform.Data.Doublets NuGet package: Platform.Data.Doublets Example | Run .NET fiddle using System; using Platform.Data; using Platform.Data.Doublets; using Platform.Data.Doublets.Memory.United.Generic; // A doublet links store is mapped to "db.links" file: using var links = new UnitedMemoryLinks<uint>("db.links"); // A creation of the doublet link: var link = links.Create(); // The link is updated to reference itself twice (as a source and a target): link = links.Update(link, newSource: link, newTarget: link); // Read operations: Console.WriteLine($"The number of links in the data store is {links.Count()}."); Console.WriteLine("Data store contents:"); var any = links.Constants.Any; // Means any link address or no restriction on link address // Arguments of the query are interpreted as restrictions var query = new Link<uint>(index: any, source: any, target: any); links.Each((link) => { Console.WriteLine(links.Format(link)); return links.Constants.Continue; }, query); // The link's content reset: link = links.Update(link, newSource: default, newTarget: default); // The link deletion: links.Delete(link); SQLite vs Doublets Deletion contracts and design Choose validation and resolution per call or through optional decorators. api/Platform.Data.Doublets.UInt64LinksTr.summary: Class UInt64LinksTransactionsLayer.Transaction Namespace Platform.Data.Doublets Assembly Platform.Data.Doublets.dll Groups link changes for commit or rollback. public class UInt64LinksTransactionsLayer.Transaction : DisposableBase, IDisposable, IDisposable Inheritance object DisposableBase UInt64LinksTransactionsLayer.Transaction Implements IDisposable IDisposable Inherited Members DisposableBase.Dispose() DisposableBase.Destruct() DisposableBase.Dispose(bool) DisposableBase.IsDisposed DisposableBase.ObjectName DisposableBase.AllowMultipleDisposeAttempts DisposableBase.AllowMultipleDisposeCalls object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Другие варианты реализации транзакций (атомарности): 1. Разделение хранения значения связи ((Source Target) или (Source Linker Target)) и индексов. 2. Хранение трансформаций/операций в отдельном хранилище Links, но дополнительно потребуется решить вопрос со ссылками на внешние идентификаторы, или как-то иначе решить вопрос с пересечениями идентификаторов. Где хранить промежуточный список транзакций? В оперативной памяти: Минусы: 1. Может усложнить систему, если она будет функционировать самостоятельно, так как нужно отдельно выделять память под список трансформаций. 2. Выделенной оперативной памяти может не хватить, в том случае, если транзакция использует слишком много трансформаций. -> Можно использовать жёсткий диск для слишком длинных транзакций. -> Максимальный размер списка трансформаций можно ограничить / задать константой. 3. При подтверждении транзакции (Commit) все трансформации записываются разом создавая задержку. На жёстком диске: Минусы: 1. Длительный отклик, на запись каждой трансформации. 2. Лог транзакций дополнительно наполняется отменёнными транзакциями. -> Это может решаться упаковкой/исключением дублирующих операций. -> Также это может решаться тем, что короткие транзакции вообще не будут записываться в случае отката. 3. Перед тем как выполнять отмену операций транзакции нужно дождаться пока все операции (трансформации) будут записаны в лог. Initial C# base: 799502ce9; merged main: c083793a. Previous PR head: 136ada5ad. Rust main: 31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b (0.13.0). No required sub-issues were listed. Other design findings are explicitly separate work per the review. a stub regression rejects unexpected existence validation Configurable missing deletion: error Existing LinksInnerReferenceExistenceValidator<T>; outer-policy tests for both backends, plain and automatic stacks Configurable missing deletion: no-op Optional LinksNonExistentDeletionResolver<T>; count, full contents, callback, search and allocator reuse assertions Preserve valid deletion/results 12 cases × four widths, bare/throw/ignore policies, both backends and optional automatic stack; Break callback, count and subsequent reuse Document C# use cases and overloads C# guide, XML contracts and executable examples/Deletion for both backends Document Rust use cases and vision Rust guide and shared design; actual limitations distinguished from intended architecture Check Rust for the original symptom Four bounded missing-delete tests: 48 combinations / 96 rejected deletions; no corruption or callbacks Audit and report other design errors separately Findings below, with existing issue references or new reports; no unrelated code fixes included Findings and separate reports Finding Evidence and disposition C# mandatory delete validation added by the old PR Reproduced by three failing tests at 136ada5ad, corrected in this PR; no invalid raw address needed C# missing-update issue proposes mandatory base checking #517; added architecture guidance to use an explicit validator or per-call check instead Rust core existence validation cannot be bypassed mem/unit/store.rs lines 504/554 and mem/split/store.rs lines 796/868; reported as #80 Rust core deletion resets even without the reset layer Same files, lines 555/872; reported separately as #81 Rust uniqueness issue proposes embedding existence validation in a resolver #66; added architecture guidance about an outer validator C# indexes are mandatory in the current memory layout Already tracked in #239 and #395; no duplicate report Rust indexing is also inseparable from the current store/liveness representation Tree fields and is_unused metadata inspected in both layouts; reported as #82 C# reuse of free slots has no append-only selection Already tracked in #172; no duplicate report Earlier C# unchecked-decorator request #51 explicitly requested omitting Ensure checks; consistent with this PR, not a new error Earlier proposal to make uniqueness checking the default #514 was closed after recognizing the optional decorator design; no new default introduced Numeric/dangling references are application-dependent #508; no global reference validation added LinksDecoratorBase forwards calls; the automatic stack does not require a validator. Explicit existence/usages/uniqueness validators, exception suppression, logging, and transactions are selectable layers, so their named behavior is not a compulsory-core-contract violation. Rust try_get_link in an explicitly chosen helper is likewise appropriate; the issue is its unavoidable use in root writes. Index detachment and split internal/external reclassification are necessary for the selected representation. Address-capacity limits are structural bounds. They were not removed or misreported as optional application validation. The audit does not claim an index-free backend or fully optional allocator is already available. Verification The three new contract tests fail against the previous PR implementation and pass after removing its mandatory checks. The baseline runner reproduces this safely with valid reset links and restores source files afterward. Experiment instructions preserve commands, finite inputs and Rust build limits. The example exercises raw, per-call, pair-based, throw, ignore, usages-reject, cascade and snapshot bulk deletion in both stores. The updated PR records final local and CI results at its final commit. Other reports above remain separate and are not acceptance criteria to implement here, as explicitly requested by the reviewer.

deletion-csharp.html.title: C# deletion contracts | Platform.Data.Doublets
deletion-csharp.html.summary: C# deletion contracts The design guidelines keep storage and application policies separate. Both UnitedMemoryLinks<T> and SplitMemoryLinks<T> expose unchecked deletion. Choose a check per call or an outer decorator when addresses may be missing. The runnable example checks the principal recipes below with both heap-backed stores: dotnet run --project examples/Deletion -c Release API and overload contracts Import Platform.Data, Platform.Data.Doublets, and Platform.Data.Doublets.Decorators for the helpers and decorators. Call on an undecorated store What it does Required caller guarantees Delete(new[] { id }, handler) Release the slot; return handler flow or Continue Live address, endpoints already reset, incoming usages handled Delete(id) Platform.Data address adapter; return deleted address from callback Same preconditions as the inner deletion; no automatic reset or missing check Delete(id, handler) Reset endpoints when Exists(id), then call inner deletion Address still must exist; missing addresses are forwarded; incoming usages handled separately EnsureLinkExists(id, name) Throw ArgumentLinkDoesNotExistsException<T> if missing No deletion; caller chooses the subsequent operation DeleteIfExists(source, target) Search by pair; delete only if found; return address or Null Endpoint reset and incoming-usage policy supplied separately Delete(id) and Delete(id, null) select different helpers. Do not infer safety from the method name alone. A handler overload returns a flow constant, not the deleted address. An ignored deletion produces no callback, so the address-returning adapter returns Null while the low-level policy returns Continue. Caller-managed fast path Use a valid live address, detach its endpoints, and resolve incoming usages in your application before releasing it. An isolated point has no other users: var id = raw.CreatePoint(); raw.Update(id, 0u, 0u); raw.Delete(new[] { id }, null); The memory backend performs no existence validation for this deletion. Never use repeated deletion of a raw address as a membership test. Zero, service constants, external references, freed slots and unallocated addresses do not satisfy the live-link precondition. AreValuesReset and EnforceResetValues also require an existing link; they are not missing-link validators. Checks for one call For a missing-address exception, validate before resetting or deleting: raw.EnsureLinkExists(id, nameof(id)); raw.Delete(id, null); // This helper supplies endpoint reset. For an address-based no-op, skip the whole operation when absent: if (raw.Exists(id)) { raw.Delete(id, null); } The existing pair-based DeleteIfExists(source, target) already skips a failed search. Wrap the raw store in NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver<T> to supply resetting before using that helper on links with non-null contents. A successful search alone does not reset endpoints or handle incoming usages. Store-wide policies Use the existing validator to reject missing deletion requests: ILinks<uint> links = new LinksInnerReferenceExistenceValidator<uint>( raw.DecorateWithAutomaticUniquenessAndUsagesResolution()); It also validates internal references in Each and Update. If that broader contract is unsuitable, choose per-call EnsureLinkExists, or implement a focused LinksDecoratorBase<T>.Delete override for your application. Use the optional ignore policy for idempotent deletion requests: ILinks<uint> links = new LinksNonExistentDeletionResolver<uint>( raw.DecorateWithAutomaticUniquenessAndUsagesResolution()); It checks existence, returns Continue without inner writes or callbacks for a missing address, and forwards an existing deletion unchanged. It does not add resetting, cascading, uniqueness or update validation. To reset without cascading, wrap raw in NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver<uint> instead of the automatic composition in these snippets. Place the chosen missing-address policy outside reset and cascade layers. Otherwise a reset resolver may read a missing link before the guard sees it. The automatic composition itself only resolves uniqueness, contents and usages; it does not promise missing-address validation. Adding a policy decorator updates the C# Facade, so recursive cascade calls re-enter the selected outer layers. If you compose both throw and ignore policies, the outer policy decides which missing requests reach the inner policy. Incoming usages and bulk operations Existence does not decide what to do with other links referencing the deleted link. Choose one of these contracts: Manage usages yourself before raw deletion, for example by removing or re-pointing references according to your data model. Reject incoming usages with LinksUsagesValidator<T>. A checked reset-only composition, outermost first, is LinksInnerReferenceExistenceValidator → NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver → LinksUsagesValidator → raw store. Self references are excluded from the usages check. Cascade usages with DecorateWithAutomaticUniquenessAndUsagesResolution() or the explicit NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver(LinksCascadeUsagesResolver(raw)) stack, and place the missing-address policy outside it. Cascading deletes other links too; C# cycle/recursion behavior is not strengthened by this PR. DeleteMany, DeleteByQuery, DeleteAllUsages, DeleteAll, and MergeAndDelete are compound helpers, not universal validators. Apply the chosen contract to every inner deletion, and account for links already removed by cascades. For bulk deletion with holes, enumerate a snapshot of actual addresses, then delete through the ignore policy (or test Exists before each call). The executable example demonstrates this. The old DeleteAll count-based loop has a separate known issue; MergeUsages also has a separate known issue. NoExceptionsDecorator suppresses exceptions; it does not undo earlier writes and cannot make an invalid unchecked deletion safe. Callback Break affects handler flow after mutation; it is not a transaction rollback. Existence checks are not synchronization: callers must prevent conflicting concurrent writes and must not mutate the store unexpectedly from callbacks between steps.

deletion-rust.html.title: Choosing a deletion contract in Rust | Platform.Data.Doublets
deletion-rust.html.summary: Choosing a deletion contract in Rust This Rust guide and the shared design guidelines live in the same PR as the C# guide, so the intended architecture is explicit for both implementations. Rust source was audited at doublets-rs main 31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b (doublets 0.13.0). Current implementation differences are documented below; C# and Rust's raw deletion contracts are not currently identical. Current APIs Import doublets::{Doublets, Links} for high-level helpers and low-level CRUD, and doublets::decorators::DecoratorsExt for compositions. Operation Current behavior delete_links(&[id], &mut handler) Both backends verify existence, reset endpoints internally, release the slot, and return Result<Flow, Error<T>> delete_with(id, handler) / delete_by_with([id], handler) Forward to low-level deletion; callback result is flow delete(id) / delete_by([id]) Return the former link address on success; propagate errors try_get_link(id) Return the link or Error::NotExists(id) without deleting get_link(id) / exist(id) Return Option<Link<T>> / membership for a per-call decision delete_all() Snapshot actual addresses and skip entries already removed by cascades delete_query_with, delete_usages_with, rebase_and_delete Compound helpers; their writes still use the selected inner stack Missing addresses currently return Error::NotExists even when all validators are omitted. This prevents the C# missing-delete corruption in the original report, but does not satisfy the design goal of an optional contract check. Do not rely on a backend check as the architectural substitute for a configured boundary. Explicit error policy For a store-wide checked boundary, use the existing existence validator: use doublets::{decorators::DecoratorsExt, mem::Global, unit, Doublets}; let mut links = unit::Store::<usize, _>::new(Global::new())? .with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution() .with_inner_reference_existence_validation(); let id = links.create_point()?; links.delete(id)?; assert!(matches!(links.delete(id), Err(doublets::Error::NotExists(x)) if x == id)); It checks deletion before forwarding, and validates internal references in updates/reads too. This makes the requested policy visible even though the current backend repeats the existence check. For one checked operation, use try_get_link(id)? before resetting or deleting instead. Ignore only a missing requested address Rust currently has no dedicated ignore-missing-deletion builder. Use a per-call helper, or a custom decorator that guards before any reset or cascade: use doublets::{Doublets, Error}; fn delete_if_exists<L: Doublets<usize>>( links: &mut L, id: usize, ) -> Result<usize, Error<usize>> { if links.exist(id) { links.delete(id) } else { Ok(0) // No writes or callbacks; zero is the default null address. } } A helper with a handler should return Ok(Flow::Continue) without calling that handler when absent. Check before the operation instead of suppressing every error afterward: an error from a later cascaded write is different from the requested address being absent. with_no_exceptions() maps all mutation errors to Flow::Break; it neither selects only missing deletions nor rolls back previous writes. For deletion by pair, call search(source, target) and delete only its Some(id) result. The endpoint-reset and usages policies still apply to the successful operation. The existence check and deletion require exclusive operation ordering; a check is not a transaction or a concurrency primitive. Contents, usages and decorator order Use .with_non_null_contents_deletion_resolution() when the selected stack should explicitly reset contents. The automatic uniqueness/usages composition includes that layer and cascading. Select .with_usages_validation() to reject incoming usages, or .with_cascade_usages_resolution() together with the reset layer to remove them. A caller-managed sequence can remove or re-point usages itself before deletion. Uniqueness is another independent choice. Rust's decorators own the layers below them and do not propagate C#'s Facade. An outer validator guards the entry operation, but is not automatically re-entered by every inner cascade. Policies needed by recursive calls must also be available below the cascading layer; inspect the composition's ordering. The automatic cascade handles its recursive resets explicitly. A user-supplied ignore wrapper should skip a missing entry before handing it to any inner resolver. Callbacks occur after the corresponding write. Flow::Break does not reverse that write or make a compound operation atomic. For bulk work, use actual addresses and account for links already removed by cascades; do not assume that count() is the largest live address. A missing-request guard does not repair an invalid mutation that has already happened. Caller-managed unchecked route: current gap The intended architecture allows a caller to guarantee a live address, detached contents and resolved usages, then call a minimal release operation without redundant contract verification or automatic resetting. Current Rust stores do not expose that route: Both update_links and delete_links call try_get_link in the backend. The missing bypass is reported in doublets-rs #80. Both backends call self.update(index, 0, 0) during deletion even if contents are already reset. Separating that policy is reported in doublets-rs #81. Removing a wrapper with into_inner() still reaches those checked/resetting backends. There is no supported delete_unchecked recipe to demonstrate at this revision. Do not manufacture one using raw pointers or claim that omitting InnerReferenceExistenceValidator removes the backend cost. Future unchecked primitives must use an appropriate Rust unsafe contract; safe public methods must preserve memory safety. These separate implementation reports remain open. Optional source/target indexing is also tracked in #82; it does not change the deletion recipes available at this revision. Reproducible examples The Rust policy probe compiles the address helper and explicit validator compositions for both backends and automatic stacks. The missing-delete probe records the current embedded-check behavior. Copy them to a checkout of the audited revision and run the bounded commands. The assertions about current backend checks are observations, not a recommendation to keep that policy in the storage root.

design.html.title: Design: storage mechanisms and optional policies | Platform.Data.Doublets
design.html.summary: Design: storage mechanisms and optional policies These guidelines apply to the C# and Rust implementations of Doublets. They record the design decision in PR #527's review. See C# deletion, Rust deletion, and the implementation audit for concrete APIs and current gaps. Core vision A user chooses the contract and cost of each layer. The storage core contains the minimum machinery necessary to represent, allocate, index and release links correctly under its documented preconditions. It does not decide what an application should do when a caller violates those preconditions. A caller who already guarantees a correct sequence of operations must be able to omit redundant contract verification. Existence validation, rejecting or ignoring missing deletions, uniqueness, usage validation or cascading, logging, and recovery are separate choices. Helpers can make those choices per call; decorators can apply them to a store. Convenient compositions must remain optional. A reset resolver supplies endpoint resetting; it must not silently become an existence validator too. The option to bypass validation is intentional. It does not promise correct results for invalid inputs. In particular, deleting a freed raw C# address can corrupt the free list, and unchecked addresses can access invalid memory. A user may take responsibility for operation ordering, or choose a checked boundary. A dangling reference or raw numeric endpoint is not automatically invalid for all applications; the configured reference and indexing model determines that. Layer responsibilities Layer Responsibility Caller choice Storage mechanism Allocate/release slots and maintain the selected representation under its preconditions Select backend and supported indexing strategy Contract validator Reject invalid addresses, usages, or duplicate values before writes Include, omit, or replace Resolver Apply a named transformation, such as reset, cascade, or ignore missing deletion Include, omit, or replace Helper Perform an explicitly requested sequence or check for one operation Choose per call Composition Offer a convenient ordered set of policies Inspect, customize, or build another stack Do not remove structural bookkeeping that makes a selected representation work. For example, detaching a freed slot from an index and classifying references for split internal/external trees are mechanisms. Rejecting a missing slot or deciding to cascade to its users are policies. Existing mandatory tree indexes and free-slot reuse have separate proposals for making their selection configurable; this PR does not claim those proposals are already implemented. Guidelines for changes in either language Write down the operation's preconditions, result, callbacks, and mutation boundary. Identify which layer owns each check or transformation. Search for existing helpers and decorators before adding checks to a root implementation. Preserve a route with no redundant validation. Keep independent policies independent. Existence, contents reset, incoming usages, uniqueness, error suppression and synchronization are not substitutes for one another. Put guards before layers that read or write the guarded link. Document order and recursive dispatch: C# propagates Facade through a stack; Rust's static decorators recurse through the layers they own. Test checked failures and no-ops for unchanged contents, allocation, count and callbacks. Test valid unchecked calls without deliberately corrupting memory. Verify that omitting a policy really omits its work. Distinguish memory safety from application validation. Rust's safe APIs must uphold Rust's safety rules. An unchecked primitive that needs caller guarantees must use an appropriate unsafe API with explicit safety conditions; do not remove checks from a safe method and create undefined behavior. In Rust, prefer generic wrappers, concrete builder return types, inlinable forwarding, and compile-time policies. In C#, keep forwarding simple and avoid making every call pay for an optional policy. Measure performance claims. Document current behavior separately from the intended architecture. When another operation violates this design, report it separately with evidence instead of expanding a focused fix into unrelated changes. These rules govern update and creation as well as deletion. Passing tests for a checked backend does not prove that validation is optional. Conversely, a crash from violating a documented unchecked precondition is not by itself a reason to make every raw operation checked.

experiments/README.html.summary: Deletion contract investigation These finite probes support issue #518 and the architecture review. Read the C# guide, Rust guide, and design/audit evidence for the selected contracts. Run from this repository root with .NET 8: dotnet test csharp/Platform.Data.Doublets.Tests -c Release \ --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~Deletion' \ --blame-hang-timeout 3m -m:1 -p:UseSharedCompilation=false dotnet run --project examples/Deletion -c Release dotnet run --project experiments/MissingDelete -c Release The 96 missing-delete theory cases select throw or ignore explicitly, for both stores and plain/automatic stacks. Each runs byte, ushort, uint and ulong addresses. Twelve valid-delete cases check callback Break with bare, throw and ignore policies. Three tests prove that the core and reset resolver omit existence validation; they only pass valid reset links. Missing/no-op checks verify contents, count, callbacks, search results and subsequent slot reuse. The trace prints allocator headers and link metadata for a valid middle deletion, optional rejection by the existing validator, reuse and following allocation. It creates at most five links per store. Raw deletions reset endpoints first. Tracing lives only in this explicit diagnostic program; library calls do not log. To reproduce the unwanted compulsory checks from the previous PR head: python3 experiments/reproduce_deletion_contract.py /path/to/dotnet The script reinstates the three mandatory checks from 136ada5ad in current source and restores every file in finally. This preserves later nullable API repairs. Run with no concurrent builds/source edits. Expected result: three failing contract tests. Only valid live/reset addresses are deleted; the probe never deliberately corrupts raw memory. Rebuild afterward to restore current binaries. The old baseline runner that deliberately submitted invalid raw addresses has been replaced. Rust observations and recipes Copy both Rust probes into a checkout of doublets-rs at the audited main revision: cp /path/to/Data.Doublets/experiments/missing_delete.rs \ doublets/tests/issue_518_missing_delete.rs cp /path/to/Data.Doublets/experiments/deletion_policies.rs \ doublets/tests/issue_518_deletion_policies.rs Build sequentially with one job, debug info disabled, a 1.75 GiB per-process address-space limit and an 8 MiB stack limit: ( ulimit -v 1835008 -s 8192 export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 cargo test -j 1 -p doublets --test issue_518_missing_delete -- --test-threads=1 cargo test -j 1 -p doublets --test issue_518_deletion_policies -- --test-threads=1 ) Verified at 31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b (0.13.0): all four missing-delete tests and both policy-example tests pass. Missing-delete coverage is 48 combinations and 96 rejected operations, with no callbacks, count/content changes or allocator corruption. The two policy tests exercise per-call ignoring and explicit outer validation with both backends and automatic stacks. These passing observations do not endorse embedded checks: Rust currently cannot omit backend existence validation or endpoint reset. Those separate design gaps are reported in #80 and #81. No Rust backend code is changed by this PR. Rust recipe code is included and verified here alongside the C# documentation, as requested by the review.

trusted-publishing.html.title: NuGet trusted publishing | Platform.Data.Doublets
trusted-publishing.html.summary: NuGet trusted publishing Both Platform.Data.Doublets (C#) and Platform.Data.Doublets.TemplateLibrary (C++) publish through GitHub Actions OIDC. Trusted publishing is always attempted first. The existing provided secrets.NUGET_TOKEN is considered only when that path is unavailable or fails. PR validation, including fork PRs, builds and consumes local packages without publishing credentials. Only non-PR execution on refs/heads/main can authenticate. Configure and verify the account Use package-registry-manager for NuGet policy management and gh-manager for generic GitHub settings. Their implementation prerequisites are tracked in package-registry-manager #72 and gh-manager #29. Those reports do not establish that setup is implemented or a policy exists. The related template migration is template #80. Authenticate to the NuGet account that creates the policy. Read its actual profile name from NuGet; do not infer it from the GitHub username or use an email address. For organization-owned policies, login uses the creator's profile name, while the policy owner is the package-owning organization. Prefer official CLI or supported API operations after checking capabilities. dotnet nuget trust manages package-signature trust, not publishing policies. Current official policy setup uses NuGet's authenticated Trusted Publishing page. When policy management is web-only, use browser-commander's authenticated profile through package-registry-manager. A sign-in page or a submitted form is not proof of a saved policy. Inspect existing policies and reuse an equivalent one. The required identity is owner linksplatform, repository Data.Doublets, workflow ci.yml (filename only). Leave the environment empty: these publishing jobs use none. Do not create a GitHub environment or a separate GitHub publisher registration. Select the NuGet user/organization that owns both package IDs. Limit allowed operations to the required package push/new-version operations. Prefer exact package selection where supported; if only a single glob is supported, use Platform.Data.Doublets*, the narrow shared prefix covering these two IDs, after auditing other matching packages. Do not use the unrestricted * glob. Re-read saved state: identity, creator, owner, scope and activation status must match. An inactive policy cannot authenticate. A temporarily active policy may need a successful publication within its activation window; report this state explicitly rather than claiming permanent activation. Through gh-manager, ensure the non-secret Actions variable NUGET_USER at a scope visible to both jobs. Read effective organization/repository precedence, preserve existing visibility restrictions, skip an equal value and re-read after writing. Do not widen global workflow permissions or rotate a legacy key to repair missing OIDC setup. What the gate verifies The credentials job checks the configured profile and tries the SHA-pinned NuGet/login with job-level id-token: write. Missing/invalid profiles are reported as trusted-publishing unavailability; failed configuration or exchange can consider the provided fallback. A username alone never proves authentication. Only those OIDC attempt steps tolerate failure; the final preflight is mandatory. No credential passes from this job to any other job. Every release caller passes the temporary NUGET_TOKEN, NUGET_LOGIN_OUTCOME and the separate NUGET_FALLBACK_TOKEN to an explicit selector. Logs identify auth=trusted-publishing|token-fallback|none, the failed step and a sanitized reason. A successful exchange selects only the temporary key, even when an expired fallback exists. Never select credentials with an empty-output expression. The former /api/v2/verifykey/{id}/{version} probe is incompatible with push-only credentials under Gallery's RequirePackageVerifyScopePolicy: HTTP 400 can occur before owner/package scope evaluation. The baseline discarded the response body, so its precise live rejection remains unconfirmed. All preflights now report package scope as unverified/unsupported instead of calling this symbols verification endpoint. Anonymous indexes must still be well formed/reachable; first publication explicitly reports that no public version exists. An index is not authentication or authorization evidence. For a provided fallback, the push-compatible POST /api/v2/package/create-verification-key/{id}/{version} authenticates the original key for push actions, even before first publication. Its returned key is discarded: Gallery replaces the subject with the requested ID, so this is never package-scope proof, and no derived key is sent to verifykey. A malformed, unsupported or unavailable authentication response fails explicitly without being called an ownership failure. Real publication enforces original package/owner permissions. HTTP error bodies are retained with bounded reads and sanitized, flattened diagnostics; credentials, raw headers and exception argv stay out of logs. The publish job downloads tested artifacts, obtains a fresh key and checks GitHub write permission before preparing/committing release metadata. C# uses that login; C++ logs in again immediately before publication, even when C# fails and C++ can independently repair its publication. Missing configuration also permits fallback here. Metadata failure prevents either package push. NuGet temporary keys last one hour and the publishing job is bounded to 40 minutes. Never move keys into artifacts, persistent secrets or cross-job outputs. Shell tracing around credentials remains forbidden. A real NuGet push rejection with HTTP 401/403 can retry once with the provided token. First inspect the anonymous exact-version download: an already public version is reported, a 404 permits retry of the same artifact, and an indeterminate result stops the retry. --skip-duplicate repairs partial package/symbol publication without rebuilding or changing versions. Authentication and both failed push outcomes remain visible. HTTP 400 package validation, transport/5xx failures, incompatible verification and build/test/doc defects cannot switch credentials. If both authentication methods fail, publication fails. Public download, mirror and release-asset failures also remain fatal. Run and recover After the code is reviewed and merged and settings are verified, execute CI on the current main revision. A rerun of an older SHA cannot load this workflow change. For settings-only repairs, restart only the affected failed CI after verified changes. Repeated setup with identical saved settings must create no duplicate policies and trigger no redundant workflow runs. Do not restart unrelated failures. Monitor exchange, per-package scope checks, package pushes, anonymous indexing checks and consumer smoke checks. Record the run ID, attempt, actual SHA, exact C#/C++ versions and final conclusion. The existing smoke jobs restore packages into isolated C# and native C++ consumers. After publication, confirm both exact versions from the public NuGet feed, then install/consume the public artifacts; cached or local artifacts are not evidence of public availability. Already-published versions remain recoverable with --skip-duplicate and no second version bump. Anonymous package indexing waits are bounded to fifteen minutes. Mirror failures remain failures while public GitHub assets can still be repaired. Do not claim release success from exchange success, username presence, an upstream issue, a package listing or a requested workflow dispatch. Retain the intentionally configured fallback after OIDC succeeds. Never delete it automatically, mint a replacement long-lived token, widen package permissions or weaken NuGet policy settings to make a release pass. The verified policy uses owner LinksPlatform, creator konard, owner/repository IDs 15116341/199508305, workflow ci.yml, no environment and exactly the two package IDs with push-only new-version permission. Preserve this setup and NUGET_USER=konard. Regression checks and references Run python3 -m unittest discover -s experiments -p 'test_*.py' -v, python3 scripts/check_repository.py and python3 scripts/check-workflows.py. experiments/test_trusted_publishing.py and experiments/test_nuget_fallback.py cover the live 400-after-exchange regression at all preflight callers, the authentication decision table, original/derived scope limits, HTTP diagnostics, first publication, expired keys and refresh, same-artifact retry, metadata ordering and credential-free PR validation. Existing publication regressions cover bounded indexing and release repair. Official NuGet trusted publishing setup and key lifetime Reviewed NuGet/login v1.2.0 source NuGet direct verification and scope evaluation Derived verification-key scope construction
